small_guidance:
- The elementwise tail is already tiny; the ConvTranspose3d dominates. Tuning the fused_hardswish kernel further (BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps) will not move fast_p meaningfully — focus iteration budget elsewhere.
- If staying small, fold the bias add back into the fused kernel (currently bias is dropped — see validity note) and keep channels_last_3d end-to-end so the epilogue reads/writes match conv output layout without a contiguous() copy.
- Add an autotune key on shape and try BLOCK_SIZE up to 32768 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3, but expect <1% gain.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output D/H/W tile) computing input × kernel outer product and scattering into the output grid with stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1 index math. This is the dominant cost (~26ms vs 8ms baseline) and the only path to fast_p>1.
- Fuse bias add, add_input, and HardSwish (v * v * clamp(v+3,0,6)/6) directly into the conv-transpose epilogue so the 4MB output tensor is written exactly once. Pre-add the learned bias into the conv bias at forward entry to save one broadcast load.
- Use channels_last_3d (NDHWC) so OC is contiguous; tile OC=64 fully in registers (since out_channels=64 fits), loop over IC*KD*KH*KW=32*27=864 as the GEMM-K with BLOCK_K=32, and use atomic-free scatter by having each output voxel gather from its contributing input voxels (i.e., implement as gather/direct-conv form: for each output (od,oh,ow), enumerate (kd,kh,kw) and check if (od+pad-kd) divisible by stride to find the input voxel — this avoids atomics entirely).
